scope: migration registry: src/concrete/MigrationRegistry.sol, src/lib/LibMigrationRegistry.sol, src/interface/IMigrationRegistryV2.sol (PR #165, namespaces)
the address registry: src/concrete/AddressRegistry.sol, src/lib/LibAddressRegistry.sol, src/interface/IAddressRegistryV1.sol
notes: Base attribution pass at f08ee42 probed 12 mutants over the pre-existing behaviours that are single-edit mutatable; 12/12 KILLED, every one by a test already on main, baseline green at 27. No pre-existing gap was found, so the tests this run added are additive rather than covering for main.

Branch pass at e26ede4 probed 18 mutants over the behaviours this run introduced; 18/18 KILLED, baseline green at 54. Those kills credit this run's own tests, because the behaviours did not exist at base.

The third candidate is absent from 'filed' because it was fixed in the same PR rather than left open: BindingTooFresh reported an age of zero for a binding stamped ahead of the clock, collapsing 'wait and retry' together with 'this chain's clock went backwards'. Split into BindingStampedInFuture. The adversarial pass found it, and a test written earlier in the run had PINNED it, which is the failure mode the skill opens with.

Process defects in this run, recorded rather than hidden: the branch pass was first run after this run's own tests were written, forfeiting attribution and requiring the base pass above as recovery; the adversarial pass was skipped on the first attempt; and the first pass ran sequentially on one checkout instead of fanning out. The base pass was then run 12-way across 12 fresh clones at 193s, against 944s for 18 sequential mutants.

Snapshot regeneration must run INSIDE the probe suite command. Mutating AddressRegistry moves its bytecode, so a stale pin makes testDeployMatchesPins and every LibAddressRegistry code-hash guard fail for every mutant regardless of behaviour, which is a universal killer that hides which test discriminates. The first attempt attributed all ten mutants to testDeployMatchesPins and was discarded.

scope: audit L01 (#264) only: LibRainDeploy's two-stage resolved-address verification
notes: Narrowed to the L01 fix, so commit and testsAfterCommit are the same tree: the tests are part of the change under test and the units did not exist before it. killedByExistingTests is 0 and gapsFilled is 0 for that reason, not because nothing was probed — 13 of 13 behaviours were probed and all 13 KILLED. The matrix establishes that each new test discriminates, not which pre-existing test covered what, and no attribution pass was possible.
B13 pins L01 itself: the deploy handing back fresh forks instead of the ones it simulated on is the defect the finding describes, and only testDeployToNetworksReturnsTheForkItDeployedOn notices it.

The probe refused to start on a red baseline, which is how a flaky suite was found rather than averaged over. The gitignored .env bound ETHEREUM_RPC_URL to eth-pokt.nodies.app and HYPEREVM_RPC_URL to rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, both measured earlier the same day as failing this suite, and the baseline moved between 668/0, 664/4 and 667/1 across runs. Repointed to tenderly for arbitrum and base and drpc for ethereum and hyperevm, after which the baseline was stable at 668 and every mutant scored.

Process defect, recorded rather than hidden: the first four mutation passes in this session — rain.deploy #260 and #262, rainix #404 and #405 — were hand-rolled mutants.toml and sed loops rather than this skill, and a subagent's sed harness ran 'git checkout -- <src>' against an uncommitted fix, reverting the fix instead of a mutant and producing 8 HARNESS-ERRORs with no evidence.
